parsed.explanation: The quoted passage is exactly where the induction breaks. With F={{1,2},{2,3}}, C={1,2}, c=1: F_c={{2,3}} and C\{c}={2}; the inductive hypothesis only describes transversals of F_c meeting {2}, so {3} is uncovered and the transversal {1,3} of F is missed by the displayed criterion. The defect is fatal, not cosmetic: the Lemma itself is false. For F_k={x_1,...,x_k,y_k} (pairwise intersecting via x_1), the sets {x_1}, {x_2,y_1}, {x_3,y_1,y_2}, ... are infinitely many minimal finite transversals, so no finite list B_1,...,B_s exists. The write-up derives its finiteness (hence L, T) solely from this false lemma; nothing else in the text supplies large-prime erasure.
